LESSON: CENTRAL PROCESSING UNIT (CPU)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: COMPUTER STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Foundation of Computer Studies
Topic 1.5: Central Processing Unit (CPU)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Central Processing Unit (CPU), part of Foundation of Computer Studies in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 COMPUTER STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How have technological advancements shaped the development of CPUs? 2) How does the CPU relate to the human brain?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Central Processing Unit (CPU) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: learner demonstrates the fetch-decode-execute cycle interaction with the CPU.

● Creativity and Imagination: learners gain new knowledge as they discuss the functions of the structural elements of the

CPU.

Values:
● Unity is promoted as learners work in pairs to create posters for use in sensitizing peers on the role of the CPU.

● Respect is enhanced as the learner understands and appreciates others’ opinions as they brainstorm the structural elements

of the CPU.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Awareness Skills: the learner develops effective communication skills while discussing the factors to consider when

selecting a CPU.

Suggested resources:

● Computer Software (Operating System and Application Program)

● Audio/visual clip

● Internet

● Screen Reader

● Magnifier

● Headphone

● Manilla papers

● Braille papers

● Permanent marker pen

● Human Resources (teachers, computer laboratory technicians).
